title: CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
chineseTitle: 第 27 章：虚荣与心灵的烦恼

paragraphs.en: Marilla walked home one late April evening after an Aid meeting, feeling the spring's joy wash over her. She noticed the vibrant fields turning from red to pale purple as the sun set. Her step lightened with the deep gladness of spring.
paragraphs.zh: 一个晚春的傍晚，玛丽拉参加完救济会后步行回家，感受到春天带来的喜悦如潮水般涌上心头。她注意到随着夕阳西下，田野的颜色从鲜红渐渐变为淡紫色。她的脚步轻快起来，心中充满了春天深深的愉悦。

paragraphs.en: Her eyes softened as she looked at Green Gables through its trees, reflecting sunlight in small glimmers. Marilla thought it was a comfort to return home to a warm fire and a nicely laid table for tea, unlike the cold evenings before Anne arrived.
paragraphs.zh: 她目光温柔地望向树丛中的绿山墙，阳光在树叶间闪烁着点点光芒。玛丽拉觉得回到家，有温暖的炉火和摆得整整齐齐的茶桌是一种安慰，这与安妮到来之前那些寒冷的夜晚大不相同。

paragraphs.en: Finding the fire out and no sign of Anne, Marilla felt disappointed and irritated. She had instructed Anne to have tea ready at five o'clock. Now, she hurried to change into her second-best dress and prepare dinner for Matthew's return from plowing.
paragraphs.zh: 找到火柴却没有见到安妮的身影，玛丽拉感到有些失望和烦躁。她曾吩咐安妮五点钟准备好茶点，现在只好赶紧换上二号礼服，准备晚餐以迎接马修从田里回来。

paragraphs.en: Marilla grumbled as she carefully carved kindling with a carving knife, more vigorously than necessary. Matthew had entered and was quietly waiting for his tea in the corner. "Anne is out somewhere with Diana, writing stories or practicing dialogues," Marilla said grimly.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉一边不满地咕哝着，一边仔细用雕刻刀切割木柴，动作比必要的情况要激烈得多。马修已经进来了，在角落里静静地等着他的茶。“安妮和戴安娜不知在哪里，要么在写故事，要么在练习对话。”玛丽拉阴沉地说。

paragraphs.en: "She never thinks about her duties. She needs to be brought back to reality suddenly."
paragraphs.zh: “她从不考虑自己的责任。需要突然把她拉回现实。”

paragraphs.en: Matthew, patient and wise, let Marilla vent without interruption. He knew from experience that she finished her work faster when left alone. "Maybe you're judging her too harshly," Matthew suggested gently.
paragraphs.zh: 马修耐心而明智，任由玛丽拉尽情发泄，没有打断她。他从经验中知道，让她独自待着时，她的工作效率更高。“或许你对她要求太严格了，”马修温和地建议道。

paragraphs.en: "Don't call her untrustworthy until you’re sure she disobeyed your instructions. Anne might have a good explanation."
paragraphs.zh: “在确定她真的违背了你的指示之前，不要轻易怀疑她的可信度。安妮或许有合理的解释。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla retorted, "She’s not here as I told her to be." She added, "I doubt she can explain that to my satisfaction. Of course, you’d take her side, Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉反驳道：“她没有按我说的去做。”她又补充了一句，“我怀疑她自己也说不清楚让我满意的原因。当然了，你肯定会站在她这边，马修。”

paragraphs.en: But it's my responsibility to raise her, not yours."
paragraphs.zh: 但这孩子由我来抚养，不是你。

paragraphs.en: It was dark when supper was ready, and Anne had not arrived. Marilla washed the dishes grimly, expecting her to come rushing across the log bridge or up Lover's Lane. Instead, she found Anne lying face-down on the bed, hidden among the pillows.
paragraphs.zh: 晚餐时分天色已晚，安妮还没有回来。玛丽拉愁眉苦脸地洗着餐具，本以为她会急匆匆地从木桥上或情人小径跑回来。没想到，她发现安妮面朝下躺在床上，被枕头遮掩得严严实实的。

paragraphs.en: "Mercy on us," said Marilla, "have you been sleeping?"
paragraphs.zh: “天哪，”玛丽拉说道，“你一直在睡觉吗？”

paragraphs.en: "No," replied Anne muffledly.
paragraphs.zh: “不，”安妮闷声闷气地回答。

paragraphs.en: "Are you sick?" asked Marilla anxiously, moving to the bed.
paragraphs.zh: “你生病了吗？”玛丽拉焦虑地问道，走到床边。

paragraphs.en: Anne cowered deeper into her pillows.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮缩回了枕头里。

paragraphs.en: "No, but please go away and don't look at me. I'm in despair and don't care about little things like class rankings or singing anymore. They're not important now because I think I'll never be able to leave this place again.
paragraphs.zh: “不，不过请你离开，别再看我了。我现在心灰意冷，对诸如班级排名或唱歌之类的小事已经毫不在意。因为我觉得自己可能永远也离不开这个地方了。”

paragraphs.en: My career is over."
paragraphs.zh: 我的事业就此终结了。

paragraphs.en: "Did anyone ever hear the like?" Marilla was bewildered. "Anne Shirley, what's wrong with you?
paragraphs.zh: “有人听说过这样的事吗？”玛丽拉感到困惑，“安妮，你怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: What have you done? Get up and tell me right away."
paragraphs.zh: 你到底做了什么？快点起来告诉我，现在就說！

paragraphs.en: Anne had slid off the bed in despair.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮绝望地从床上滑了下来。

paragraphs.en: "Look at my hair," she whispered.
paragraphs.zh: “看看我的头发，”她低声说道。

paragraphs.en: Marilla lifted her candle to examine Anne’s hair, which flowed down her back in heavy masses. It was a strange green color, with streaks of red making it even more ghastly.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉举起蜡烛仔细查看安妮的头发，只见她的头发如瀑布般垂落在背后，浓密厚重。颜色奇异偏绿，还夹杂着红色条纹，显得更加令人不安。

paragraphs.en: "It's green!" exclaimed Marilla. "Anne Shirley, what have you done to your hair?
paragraphs.zh: “是绿色的！”玛丽拉惊叫道，“安妮·谢里登，你把头发染成绿色了？”

paragraphs.en: It's a queer, dull, bronzy green."
paragraphs.zh: 这是一种奇怪而单调的铜绿色。

paragraphs.en: "Yes, it’s green," moaned Anne. "I thought nothing could be worse than red hair, but now I know green is ten times worse. Oh, Marilla, you can't imagine how wretched I am."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，它是绿色的，”安妮呻吟道，“我以为没有什么能比红头发更糟糕了，但现在我知道绿色糟糕得多。哦，玛丽拉，你无法想象我现在有多痛苦。”

paragraphs.en: "I'll find out how you got into this mess," said Marilla. "Come down to the kitchen—it's too cold up here—and tell me what you've done. You haven’t caused trouble for over two months, and I was sure another one was coming."
paragraphs.zh: “我得弄清楚你闯了什么祸。”玛丽拉说，“下来到厨房吧，这里暖和些。你得告诉我究竟是怎么回事。两个月来你还从来没惹过麻烦，我还以为这次又躲不过去了呢。”

paragraphs.en: Anne admitted she had dyed her hair, explaining it was a small act of wickedness to get rid of her red hair. Marilla sarcastically pointed out that if Anne had decided to dye her hair, she should have chosen a decent color instead of green. Anne defended herself, saying the peddler assured her the dye would turn her hair black and that she believed him implicitly.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮承认自己染了头发，解释说这是为了摆脱红发而做出的一个小小的恶作剧。玛丽拉讽刺地说，如果安妮真的决定染发，应该选择一个体面的颜色，而不是绿色。安妮为自己辩护，说卖货郎保证染发后她的头发会变黑，并且她完全相信他的话。

paragraphs.en: Marilla asked who said this, and Anne replied it was the peddler who visited earlier in the day. Marilla expressed frustration at having allowed the peddler into the house, warning against encouraging such visits.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉问是谁说的，安妮回答说是那天早些时候来过这里的叫卖商。玛丽拉抱怨自己让叫卖商进了屋，警告不要鼓励这种来访。

paragraphs.en: Anne refused to let Gilbert into the house, remembering what Marilla had told her. She went outside and examined his items on the doorstep. He was a German Jew, not an Italian, working hard to bring his family from Germany.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮没有让吉尔伯特进屋，她想起了玛丽拉曾经对她说的话。她走到外面，在门口检查了他的那些物品。原来他是个德国犹太人，并非意大利人，正努力工作要把家人从德国接过来。

paragraphs.en: His earnest talk about them moved Anne, prompting her to buy something to help him. Suddenly, she noticed a bottle of hair dye that promised beautiful black hair. The temptation was strong, but it cost seventy-five cents and she only had fifty left.
paragraphs.zh: 他诚恳地谈起那些事情，让安妮深受触动，促使她决定买点东西来帮助他。就在这时，她突然注意到一瓶承诺能让头发变得乌黑亮丽的染发剂。虽然诱惑很大，但那瓶染发剂要价七十五美分，而她只剩下五十美分了。

paragraphs.en: She bought the bottle and applied it with an old brush as directed. After using up the entire bottle, Anne regretted her decision when she saw the awful color. She repented immediately and has been doing so ever since.
paragraphs.zh: 她买下了那瓶染发剂，并按照指示用旧刷子涂了起来。等用完了整瓶之后，安妮看到自己变成的可怕颜色时后悔不已。自那以后，她一直感到懊悔。

paragraphs.en: Marilla sternly hoped Anne would repent genuinely and see where vanity had led her. They decided to wash Anne's hair thoroughly, but it remained red despite vigorous scrubbing. The peddler’s claim that the dye wouldn’t wash off proved true.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉严厉地希望安妮能真心悔改，认识到虚荣心把她引向了何方。她们决定彻底给安妮洗头，但尽管用力搓揉，头发依旧红得刺眼。那卖货郎声称染料不会轻易洗掉的话果真应验了。

paragraphs.en: Anne's despair over her dyed hair persisted for a week. She stayed indoors and shampooed her hair daily. Diana alone knew the secret but promised not to reveal it.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮因染发而感到的绝望情绪持续了一个星期。她整天待在室内，每天都要洗头。只有戴安娜一人知道真相，但她答应不会泄露出去。

paragraphs.en: Marilla finally declared, "Your hair must be cut off; there is no other choice." Anne reluctantly agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉终于说道：“你的头发必须剪掉，别无选择。”安妮不情愿地答应了。

paragraphs.en: With tears in her eyes, she took out the scissors. "Please do this quickly," she pleaded. "I feel as if my heart were breaking.
paragraphs.zh: 她眼里含着泪，拿出了剪刀。“求你快点做吧，”她恳求道，“我觉得我的心都要碎了。”

paragraphs.en: This is such an unromantic misfortune. Girls in books lose their hair for good reasons, but losing it because of a bad dye job seems so tragic."
paragraphs.zh: 这真是个如此不浪漫的不幸。书中的女孩们因为正当的理由失去头发，但因为染发失败而失去头发未免太悲惨了。

paragraphs.en: Marilla cut the hair swiftly. Anne wept during the process, feeling her heart break. When she looked in the mirror later, she was devastated by Marilla's thorough work.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉迅速地剪着头发，安妮在过程中不禁泪流满面，感觉心如刀割。事后照镜子时，她对玛丽拉彻底修剪的结果感到极度失望和沮丧。

paragraphs.en: The result was unflattering, and Anne vowed never to look at herself again until her hair grew back.
paragraphs.zh: 结果颇为尴尬，安妮发誓在头发长回来之前再也不照镜子了。

paragraphs.en: Finally, she turned the glass away from her face. "I'll never see myself until my hair grows," she declared passionately.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，她把镜子从脸上移开。“得等我的头发长出来才能再看看自己了，”她热情地宣称。

paragraphs.en: Anne decided to wear her hair short as penance for being vain. She would look at herself every time she entered her room and see how unattractive she appeared, without trying to imagine otherwise. Her red, long, curly hair had made her feel beautiful, but now she realized it was a vanity.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮决定剪短头发作为虚荣的赎罪。她每次进房间都会照镜子，看着自己那不再引人注目的样子，不再试图想象其他。她那红红的、长长的卷发曾让她觉得自己美丽无比，但现在她意识到那只是虚荣罢了。

paragraphs.en: On Monday, Anne's short haircut caused a sensation in school, though no one guessed the true reason. Josie Pye commented that Anne looked like a scarecrow, and Anne forgave her without saying anything back. She felt virtuous for forgiving others.
paragraphs.zh: 星期一，安妮那短短的发型在学校引起了不小的轰动，但没有人猜到其中的真实原因。乔西·皮伊评论说安妮看起来像一个稻草人，而安妮没有回嘴，只是心中暗自觉得宽恕他人是一种美德。

paragraphs.en: Anne vowed to focus all her energies on being good from then on and never try to be beautiful again. She believed it was better to be good, even though sometimes it was hard to believe. She intended to grow up to be a credit to Marilla and Mrs. Allan, just like Miss Stacy.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮发誓从此要把所有精力都放在做好人上，再也不企图美丽了。她相信即使有时候很难做到，做个好人总是更好的。她打算长大后不辜负玛丽拉和艾伦太太的期望，就像斯泰西小姐一样。

paragraphs.en: Diana suggested tying a black velvet ribbon with a bow around Anne's head when her hair grew back. Anne decided to call it a snood, finding the term romantic. Despite talking too much, she hoped Marilla wouldn't mind; Marilla's headache had improved but was still bad earlier that afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜建议等安妮的头发长回来后，在头上系一根黑色丝绒带子打个蝴蝶结。安妮觉得这个叫“snood”听起来很有浪漫气息，便决定这么称呼它。尽管她说话还是太多，但希望玛丽拉不要介意；那天下午早些时候，玛丽拉的头痛有所缓解，但仍不算太好。

paragraphs.en: Marilla mentioned she would see a doctor about her worsening headaches and that she didn’t mind Anne’s chatter, having grown accustomed to it.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉提到她打算去看医生，因为头痛越来越严重，并且她不介意安妮的喋喋不休，已经习惯了她的絮叨。
